text: A relation ≺ is well-founded if and only if it admits no infinite ___ chain a₀ ≻ a₁ ≻ a₂ ≻ ⋯.
explanation: Well-foundedness is equivalent to the absence of an infinite descending chain; this is what guarantees that recursive definitions and inductive proofs over ≺ terminate and are valid. The pitfall f(n) = f(n+1) fails precisely because it 'descends' upward rather than downward.
